Photo: Handout Iran Fuel tanker explosion kills 11 in traffic accident near Sanandaj RUDAW English 05-09-2026 Listen Listen 0:00 0:00 Text Size RUDAW English 05-09-2026 Related Articles Iran 07-09-2026 Iran accuses US, EU of nuclear pressure as IAEA seeks site access Iran 07-09-2026 Iran identifies two suspects in assault on Iraqi students as Baghdad opens investigation Iran 07-09-2026 As Iran’s formal trade routes choke, Kurdish border trade surges ERBIL, Kurdistan Region - At least 11 people were killed and seven others injured on Saturday evening when a fuel tanker collided with a passenger car on the main Hamadan-Sanandaj highway in Iran’s Kurdistan province, according to local officials and state media. The accident occurred at around 5 pm near the entrance to Sanandaj, with the tanker immediately bursting into flames and damaging several other vehicles, according to state media. Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported that the crash “led to the explosion of a fuel tanker” and initially put the death toll at 10. “The Head of the Emergency and Pre-Hospital Medical Center of Kurdistan University of Medical Sciences” said 10 people had died following the accident, according to IRIB. Most of the victims’ bodies were reportedly completely burned in the fire. The governor of Sanandaj has declared two days of public mourning following the deadly crash. The incident comes as Iran continues to record a high number of road fatalities. More than 19,500 people were killed in traffic accidents across the country during the Iranian year that ended on March 20, according to official figures from Iran’s Legal Medicine Organization. The toll was slightly higher than the 19,435 road deaths recorded the previous year, according to Iran’s state news agency ISNA.
